description: A composite eight-panel figure mixing two modalities: four EBSD boundary/twin maps (a–d) and four TEM images (e–h). Panels (a–d) are EBSD maps of Fe30Mn(x)Al1C with (a) 8% Al, (b) 10% Al, (c) 11% Al and (d) 12% Al; each carries a 200 µm scale bar and all share the bottom legend: black line = θ>15°, red line = Twin boundary, green line = BCC phase. Panels (a–c) show equiaxed austenite grains densely intersected by straight, parallel red twin boundaries with no green BCC lines, whereas (d) alone adds green BCC-phase bands and visibly finer austenite grains. (e) is a bright-field TEM image of the 8% Al steel (20 nm scale bar) whose inset SAED pattern is indexed (000), (020)γ, (200)γ, showing only γ reflections; (f) and (g) are dark-field TEM images of the 10% and 11% Al steels (20 nm scale bars) whose SAED insets contain additional (010)κ and (100)κ spots marked by yellow boxes, with fine scattered κ-carbide particles; (h) is the dark-field image of the 12% Al steel with a 100 nm scale bar showing markedly coarser, brighter κ-carbide particles. The group demonstrates that increasing Al refines the austenite grain, introduces a small BCC/ferrite fraction only at 12% Al, and drives κ-carbide precipitation from absent at 8% Al to coarse at 12% Al.

subfigures.description: EBSD boundary map of the 8% Al steel, 200 µm scale bar; equiaxed austenite grains cut by abundant straight parallel red twin boundaries; no green BCC-phase lines visible.
EBSD boundary map of the 10% Al steel, 200 µm scale bar; same equiaxed austenite plus dense red twin boundaries, no green BCC lines.
EBSD boundary map of the 11% Al steel, 200 µm scale bar; twinned austenite grains, no green BCC-phase lines.
EBSD boundary map of the 12% Al steel, 200 µm scale bar; adds green BCC-phase (ferrite) bands crossing the map and the austenite grains appear finer than in (a–c).
Bright-field TEM image of the 8% Al steel, 20 nm scale bar, featureless/speckled matrix; inset SAED pattern indexed (000), (020)γ and (200)γ with no κ-carbide spots.
Dark-field TEM image of the 10% Al steel, 20 nm scale bar, showing fine bright κ-carbide particles; inset SAED with (000), (020)γ, (200)γ plus κ spots (010)κ and (100)κ marked by yellow boxes.
Dark-field TEM image of the 11% Al steel, 20 nm scale bar, showing fine bright κ-carbide particles; inset SAED with γ and κ reflections, the κ spots boxed in yellow.

Dark-field TEM image of the 12% Al steel, 100 nm scale bar (ten times the magnification scale of e–g), showing distinctly larger and brighter κ-carbide particles; inset SAED with (000), (020)γ, (200)γ and boxed κ spots.

observations.observation: The bottom legend of the EBSD maps defines three line types exactly as printed: black line = θ>15°, red line = Twin boundary, green line = BCC phase.
Each of panels (a–d) contains a 200 µm scale bar.
Green (BCC phase) boundary lines are present only in panel (d), the 12% Al map; panels (a), (b) and (c) contain black and red lines only.
Panels (e), (f) and (g) each carry a 20 nm scale bar, whereas panel (h) carries a 100 nm scale bar.
The SAED inset in panel (e) shows only γ reflections labelled (000), (020)γ and (200)γ, with no additional κ reflections.

The SAED insets in panels (f), (g) and (h) contain extra diffraction spots labelled (010)κ and (100)κ, highlighted by small yellow/orange square boxes, in addition to the (020)γ, (200)γ and (000) reflections.
Caption states that (a–d) are EBSD maps showing grain and twin boundary (Σ3) arrangement together with the BCC phase fraction for 8%, 10%, 11% and 12% Al.
Caption states that (e) is a bright-field TEM image with inset SAED pattern of the 8% Al sample showing an absence of signal from the κ-carbide phase.

Caption states that (f–h) are dark-field TEM images showing the κ phase for 10%, 11% and 12% Al, each taken along the [001]γ zone axis using one of the κ-carbide diffraction spots shown in the inset SAED images.
Citing text states that for Al contents of 8–11% only a single austenite phase is present, while a small ferrite volume fraction of 3.1% was observed in the 12% Al low-density steel.
Citing text reports average grain sizes of about 28.3 µm, 29.7 µm and 23.7 µm for the 8%, 10% and 11% Al steels, and a significantly smaller austenite grain size of 12.6 µm for the 12% Al steel.

Citing text states that no κ-carbides were observed in the 8% Al steel, whereas extensive κ-carbide formation occurred for Al contents of 10% and larger, with average κ-carbide diameters of about 1 nm, 1.5 nm and 15 nm for 10%, 11% and 12% Al respectively.

The fine κ-carbide precipitate contrast in the 20 nm dark-field panels (f) and (g) is consistent with the reported nanometre-scale diameters, while the much larger bright particles in the 100 nm panel (h) correspond to the reported coarsening at 12% Al; only relative size contrast is visible, no values are printed on the panels.
Panels (a–d) do not print the BCC phase fraction numerically; the maps show only boundary-line types, so the quantified ferrite fraction comes from the citing text, not from the pixels.

unreadable_items: The SAED inset diffraction-spot labels in (e)–(h) are rendered very small; spot positions and the (010)κ/(100)κ box highlights are visible but the indices are only partially readable at the supplied resolution
Panels (a–d) carry no printed numerical BCC phase fraction or grain-size values; these values appear only in the citing text
